figures.alt: Historic wood double-hung window with localized sill repair and retained surrounding trim
figures.caption: Historic work starts with a condition-based scope. Repairability, water path, retained material, and visible character all affect what should be proposed for review.

figures.alt: Residential interior with wood header, adjustable steel temporary support posts, opened framing, and protected floor
figures.caption: Older homes can reveal consequential structural conditions after finishes open. Engineering, temporary support, connections, and the final framing sequence need to be understood before demolition advances.
figures.before: Structural Realities in Riverside and Avondale Homes

figures.alt: Renovation planning table with abstract drawings, material samples, and a blank notebook
figures.caption: A useful renovation budget separates investigation, permits, structural work, services, envelope repairs, finishes, and contingency rather than relying on a generic square-foot number.
